title: adaptive-field-indexer-and-trace-affinity-router-for-multiformat-log-ingest
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: our current ingest pipeline indexes an unbounded set of JSON fields for structured logs which drives indexing cost and high-cardinality label explosions in Loki/ES. Additionally, logs belonging to the same distributed trace sometimes land in different hot shards which complicates low-latency trace-centered queries and join operations.

Goal: implement an adaptive field indexer that performs tenant-aware schema fingerprinting and hot-field selection at ingest time, combined with a trace-affinity router that keeps log fragments from the same trace grouped into the same hot-path storage shard. The solution should reduce indexing cost, keep recent trace-centric queries fast (<2s for 95th percentile for 1h window), and retain the ability to run full-text or deep queries against cold objects in blob storage.

Scope: ingest normalization -> schema fingerprinting -> hot-field selector -> index router (Loki hot path + ES/secondary index for search) -> cold-path compressed JSON blobs in object store. Ensure correlation-id/trace-id propagation is preserved end-to-end and used as a primary affinity key for routing when present.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline accepts mixed JSON/plaintext logs and normalizes to canonical envelope with tenant_id, trace_id, timestamp, severity, message, and meta fields.
Adaptive field indexer selects <= 12 hot fields per tenant by default, with adaptive increase/decrease based on query frequency and cardinality heuristics.
Trace-affinity router ensures >= 99% of log records that share trace_id within a 30s write window are routed to same hot shard.
Recent trace query (trace_id lookup across last 1 hour) returns full correlated log set in <2s p95 for canary tenants.
End-to-end ingestion throughput >= 50k log records/sec in benchmark with 20% structured JSON payloads and 80% plaintext for canary configuration.
Indexing cost for hot path reduces estimated per-tenant token/label cardinality cost by >= 25% compared to baseline on pilot tenants.
No tenant can cause index blowup beyond its configured cardinality budget; protection circuits are validated in chaos tests.
Rollout plan (canary -> staged) documented and automated with feature flag gating and rollback hooks.
implementation_notes: Component diagram: Ingest Gateway -> Normalizer -> Schema Fingerprinter -> Hot Field Selector -> Router -> (Loki hot shards + ES index consumers + S3 cold blob writer).
Schema fingerprint: short hash of sorted top-level keys and labeled nested paths sampled for first N records per tenant; stored in metadata service with TTL and revision history.

Hot-field selection heuristic: combine query frequency (from query logs), cardinality estimator (HyperLogLog), and stability score (field presence consistency). Default cap 12 fields per tenant with override via tenant config.

Trace-affinity routing: use trace_id primary, fallback to tenant-consistent-hash on envelope id. Implement small in-memory routing table on ingest node with LRU eviction and sticky shard assignment for 30s windows.

Backpressure: when hot-shard queue depth crosses threshold, demote selected fields temporarily and switch routing to gracefull degrade mode writing more to cold-path only; emit observability metrics and alerts.
Metadata sync: expose API for Console to show selected hot fields per tenant, and allow admin to pin/unpin fields for short-term experiments.
Cost accounting: tag hot-field writes separately for per-tenant billing and propagate per-token/label counters into billing pipeline.
Compatibility: ensure existing Loki label conventions remain compatible; provide an optional ES ingest transformer to flatten hot fields with controlled mapping templates.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting, aligned on goals and ACs. Assigned infra and data-sci owners.
2026-03-12: Prototype of schema fingerprint service completed (nodejs) and validated on 24-hour sample logs; fingerprint collisions <0.2%.
2026-03-13: Hot-field selection algorithm v1 implemented using query-sampled rankings and HLL cardinality; local benchmark shows 30% reduction in unique labels for sample tenant.
2026-03-14: Trace-affinity router prototype integrated with a single ingest node; end-to-end tests show 98.7% co-location of trace fragments within 30s window — need to tighten to 99% target.
Next: implement shard sticky-timers and small-ring replication to reach 99% target; add chaos tests for node failover.
test_plan: Unit tests for schema fingerprint collisions and HLL cardinality components.
Integration test: end-to-end ingest of mixed payloads with synthetic traces (100k traces/hour) asserting co-location and query latency.
Load test in staging with 200k rps simulated across 200 tenants; measure queue depth, ingest latency, and write amplification to ES/Loki.
Chaos test: kill single hot-shard node and validate routing table reconvergence within 5s and no data loss to cold store.
Cost regression test: compare estimated storage and indexing cost vs baseline for pilot tenants over 7 days.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged deployment: enable schema fingerprinting and hot-field indexing in staging only.
Canary group: select 10 low-risk tenants with varied cardinality profiles; enable trace-affinity routing for them.
Observability gates: p95 ingest latency < 300ms, trace co-location >= 99%, error rate < 0.2% for canary.
Staged ramp: 10% tenants -> 40% -> 100% over 3 weeks with monitoring and manual hold points.
Rollback: toggle feature flag off which switches to current full-indexing ingest path and replays buffered data to cold store.
rollback_plan: Immediate toggle of feature flag to disable hot-field selection and affinity routing.
Fallback writes to full indexing path; ensure migrations run to rehydrate any temporary metainfo.
Automated alerting triggers rollback on SLO breach; run postmortem and patch before next attempt.
open_questions: How should we surface per-tenant hot-field suggestions in Console without exposing high-cardinality sensitive keys? (privacy/legal review required)
What default retention should cold blobs have for tenants that expect long-tail forensic queries? (team policy + cost model)
Should trace-affinity be optional for tenants that actively use cross-shard stream joins?
Operational: what's the expected memory footprint of the in-memory routing table at 10k concurrent sticky entries per ingest node?
risks_mitigations: Risk: cardinality explosion from mis-selected hot fields -> Mitigation: cap hot fields, use HLL and sample-driven backoff; implement circuit breaker to demote fields.
Risk: trace-affinity stickiness causes hotspots -> Mitigation: use small ring replication and allow shard spillover after threshold; monitor shard queue depth and auto-balance.
Risk: schema drift invalidates fingerprinting -> Mitigation: maintain fingerprint versions and fall back to sampling+recompute; alert on sudden churn.
Risk: increased operational complexity for support -> Mitigation: expose clear console controls, per-tenant diagnostics, and automated runbooks.
